parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs strong state-level protections with unavoidable federal exposures. The state prohibits public-accommodation discrimination, enhances bias penalties, offers X state IDs, and shields lawful care for arriving patients, but it cannot cancel federal passport/entry screening, federal-facility sex-by-birth rules, federal investigations, or federal custody practices. Document discrepancy at entry can lead to refusal and a possible permanent fraud finding, and federal custody has documented hormone denial, forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. Litigation and local protections mitigate daily exposure, yet the operative federal tier-one exposures remain unremedied.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal policy issues M/F only for new passports, allows restriction to take effect, and instructs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support lifetime fraud ineligibility. Passports have been confiscated/blocked, stranding some travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist. Passport policy remains litigated.
entry_documents.interaction: State X licences/birth certificates do not override federal visa/passport adjudication; a state-accepted document can still trigger federal entry refusal or investigation.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections adopted a model mandating short haircuts, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Number of trans prisoners stopped being reported in 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Several orders have been blocked or enjoined, but no effective remedy for custody practices is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry discrepancy can lead to investigation or detention, after which federal birth-sex/custody practices apply regardless of state protective law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Many other states ban facility access, and some make it a trespass offence with a documented arrest and 24-hour men's-ward detention.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The rated state is in the most-protective tier, has no documented bathroom ban in the dossier, and its anti-discrimination law covers public accommodation, education and public services uniformly.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection governs state/local venues but does not cancel federal-facility restrictions or criminal trespass regimes elsewhere a traveller may enter.

care_services.exposure: National orders target gender-affirming care for minors, propose barring public insurance for under-18 trans patients, and federal authorities subpoenaed hospitals for minors' records. Federal custody denial of hormones is documented.
care_services.protection: State shield law signed 13 July 2023 protects patients and providers from civil/criminal investigation for care legal in-state but banned at home; public coverage of gender-affirming care is established.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects in-state care access for arriving families, but federal funding, investigation and custody rules can still interact with treatment, records and medication.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal guidance invokes 'radical gender ideology' in extremism framing and a cash-reward system; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as 'radically pro-transgender'. An order directs investigation/prosecution over facilitating a minor's social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity and some executive orders are enjoined; the state adds enhanced penalties and abolished gay/trans panic defences.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State hate-crime and panic-defence protections improve local recourse but do not neutralise federal threat-framing, investigations or enforcement priorities.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders characterising youth care as mutilation, directing prosecution of teachers for names/pronouns, and proposed insurance bans create risk for travelling minors and guardians seeking or continuing transition-related support.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law expressly protects patients arriving from banning jurisdictions, and state law prohibits discrimination in public education and services.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family may obtain shielded in-state care while remaining exposed to federal investigation, records demands, school-policy disputes and federal facilities rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2025 polling found 66% support for assigned-sex documentation and 69% for birth-sex sports rules; bias crimes are a recurring share of hate incidents nationally. No state-specific police-stop or prosecution data was located.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State bias-motivated violence carries enhanced penalties, anti-discrimination law is statewide, and public-accommodation protection covers daily visitor settings.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local recourse is stronger than in banning states, but federal hostility and national public framing may increase confrontation, while enforcement in practice is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport, executive-order and health-rule challenges are unresolved; enforcement of the state public-accommodations law against excluding venues, custody treatment and airport screening are deliberately not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented state statutes, shield law, enhanced penalties and court challenges provide partial recourse, but their visitor-facing operation is unevenly evidenced.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved federal litigation means exposure depends on rules in effect at travel; state remedies cannot cure entry refusal, federal facility exclusion or federal custody placement.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: a universal birth-sex facility/document regime applies despite polite local treatment, and complaints do not reliably secure access. This case is slightly lower overall because entry discrepancy may cause refusal/permanent fraud consequences and federal custody abuse is documented, partly offset by strong state daily protections.

Lower than this anchor is not warranted: 0.35-E has a local clinic birth-sex rule with repeated humiliation and no change. Here the hostile rule is federal rather than local, so the state shield and anti-discrimination law improve post-entry daily life, but they cannot displace entry, federal facilities or custody exposures.

Higher than this anchor is not warranted: 0.65-A has no universal facility ban, accepts foreign markers, and shows working refunds, training and convictions. Here federal screening, passport restrictions and custody practices remain operative exposures, so the case sits materially below reduced-risk despite protective state law.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's journey is sequential: federal entry and document screening is the first gate and can produce refusal, stranding or fraud investigation; federal facilities and any detention then apply federal rules. If admitted, the state's most-protective framework materially improves hotels, services, education, bias-crime penalties and shielded care, especially for minors. Those protections are real but territorially and institutionally limited. Because the harshest operative federal exposures are universal and not shown to be remedied, while local protections work only after entry and outside federal control, the combined regime falls in elevated risk, near the 0.45 universal-exposure anchor.
